_purpose: Per-category rubrics for the LLM-as-judge step (Phase 14). The judge takes (goal, output) and asks an LLM to score the output 0-100 against these rubrics. Compared to Phase 12's mechanical checks (length/format/refusal), this catches semantic failures: 'agent wrote 500 words but the content is gibberish'. Each rubric is a short bullet list; the judge LLM scores against them.

default._doc: Catch-all rubric. Applied when no category-specific entry exists. Keep it conservative so we don't false-positive on simple tasks.
criteria: Answer is on-topic — addresses what the user actually asked.
Answer is coherent — sentences make grammatical sense.
No obvious factual errors or self-contradictions.
Length is appropriate for the request (not absurdly short or long).
If the user asked for a file or specific format, the output matches.
Output is a substantive piece of writing on the requested topic.
Structure is appropriate (intro / body / conclusion or sections).
Length roughly matches the requested word count if specified.
Claims are coherent — no obvious nonsense or filler like 'lorem ipsum'.
If a citation source was provided, the output references it.
Document body actually contains substantive content (not just the prompt repeated).
Sections/slides/rows have meaningful headings + content.
Length is in the right ballpark vs the user's specification.
Language matches user's request (Chinese in, Chinese out).

image_generation._doc: Image generation can't be judged textually — fall through to mechanical checks only. Threshold high enough that the judge effectively passes for any artifact.
criteria: An image artifact was produced (file exists, non-empty).

unknown._doc: Chat / Q&A / freeform. Most user requests fall here.
criteria: The reply answers the user's question directly.
Reply matches user's language.
No placeholder text ('I'll answer that:', 'as an AI...', etc.).
No factual hallucinations the user would obviously notice.
Length is appropriate (one-liner Q gets one-liner A; deep Q gets fuller A).

judge_call._doc: Knobs for how the judge LLM is invoked. max_tokens kept low because the judge response is a short JSON object, not prose. temperature=0 for determinism — we want consistent scores across reruns of the same content.
